# Moving the bread order cut-off

Customers could order sourdough for next-day pickup until 9pm. From next
Monday the cut-off is 6pm. This note is for the counter staff, since you'll
get the questions.

## What kept going wrong

The ovens start at four in the morning. Whoever opens up prints the order
sheet at half past three and portions the dough from it. Anything ordered
after the sheet came off the printer got missed, which last month happened
on about one morning in five, mostly after late orders from the café on Mill
Street. Each time, someone had to phone the customer, apologise, and offer a
different loaf. Nobody enjoyed those calls.

Printing the sheet later doesn't help. The rye needs a longer rest than
anything else we bake, so the baker would be starting it with half the
orders still unknown.

## The new cut-off

Online orders close at 6pm. Phone orders close at the same time, and I've
asked everyone on the counter to stop taking them after that, even for
regulars. The sheet now prints itself at 6:05 and goes to the kitchen tablet
as well as the printer.

Anything later rolls over to the following day. The confirmation email says
so in its first line.

## What I expect

Fewer missed loaves, obviously. I'd also guess we lose a few orders from
people who decide at eight in the evening that they want bread for
breakfast. Probably not very many. Last month 31 of roughly 700 orders came
in after six. Most of those were from the café, who have already told us the
earlier time suits them better. That part seems fine.

One thing I haven't solved is the Saturday market stall. It still takes its own
orders in a paper notebook. The notebook reaches the bakery whenever someone remembers to
drop it off, which can be Sunday afternoon. That needs a separate fix,
probably a shared form on the stall's phone, so I've left it out of this
change.

If the counter hears complaints, write them in the book by the till with the
date, and I'll read through it at the end of the month to see whether late
orders turn out to be worth more than the missed loaves cost us. If they
are, the cut-off goes back to 9pm.
